title: Domantas Sabonis Trade Buzz Picks Up as Eastern Conference Contender Enters the Picture - NewsBreak
text:
By Shabiha Akter ,
1 hours ago
Domantas Sabonis (Image Credits: Imagn) The Sacramento Kings are now sitting among the NBA’s worst teams with a disappointing 12-36 record. Even the star trio of Domantas Sabonis, DeMar DeRozan, and Zach LaVine has struggled to lift the team into serious contention. Reportedly, Sacramento is now preparing for a full-scale fire sale ahead of the trade deadline.
For teams around the league in need of a reliable starting center, this situation is a prime opportunity to pursue Sabonis. According to Sam Amick of The Athletic, the Toronto Raptors have emerged as a serious and credible landing spot for the Kings’ big man, with RJ Barrett potentially heading to Sacramento in return.
“ While Washington, Phoenix, and Chicago are known to have had some interest in Sabonis, league sources confirmed reports that Toronto is a legitimate possibility as we approach the deadline. It’s worth noting that the Raptors’ RJ Barrett, who is owed $27.7 million this season and $29.6 million next season, was drafted No. 3 overall out of Duke by current Kings general manager Scott Perry in 2019, when Perry held the same position with the Knicks. The two old friends shared a warm hug and extended conversation before the game at Golden 1 Center .”
Although Washington, Phoenix, and Chicago have also emerged as potential suitors, the report suggests that Toronto’s interest stands out as particularly serious . The Raptors’ pursuit of Sabonis makes sense, given their ongoing struggles to get consistent production from the center spot. However, a previous report from Marc Stein indicated that Sacramento is not keen on taking back long-term contracts that Toronto could offer in return.
Sacramento Holding Firm on Domantas Sabonis Trade Price Domantas Sabonis (Image Credits: Imagn) According to HoopsHype, Sacramento has made its asking price clear in discussions involving Domantas Sabonis. The franchise is seeking a first-round draft pick in any potential trade.
“In trade talks involving Sabonis, the Kings told at least one interested team that they’d like a first-round team in return, HoopsHype has learned ,” the report read.
Sabonis remains one of the NBA’s most skilled passing big men. Hence, it is reasonable for the Kings to demand a significant return that could aid their long-term rebuild.
After missing 27 games with a left knee injury, Sabonis rejoined the Kings’ lineup earlier this month. So far this season, he is averaging 15.5 points, 11.4 rebounds, and 4.2 assists per game.
At this point, it increasingly feels like Sabonis’ time in Sacramento may be nearing its end. Let’s see which team ultimately wins the race to acquire him.
